brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;half-n with piece:0,0,1;half-n stacked on it, joined by a snap, plus a top cover and end caps
drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:1#0,0#cut, one per storey

The drawers and the top cover give storage space. Only the top drawer and top cover hold workshop props (a marker, a pen and a roll of gaffer tape); the lower drawer refused every small item I tried. The configurator checks fit only, not strength or load ratings.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey storage tower with two drawers: two north-half hex bases stacked one on the other, each with a drawer in its cut face. The top has a cover and every open face has a solid end cap. When I tried to lock the joints, the configurator said there was nothing to change. check_build found no issues and the mesh-collision check came back clear. For staging, the top drawer holds a marker and a pen standing up, and a roll of gaffer tape sits on the top cover. The lower drawer has no props: its compartments refused every small item I tried, and there wasn't enough headroom for taller ones. Both drawers are shown open. I can't speak to strength or load capacity for workbench use, because the configurator only checks fit.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
